Volvo Announces Refreshed XC40, EX40, EC40 Pricing for the UK, Also the XC90 T8 Long Range PHEV
50 photos
Photo: Volvo
Volvo Car UK aims to conquer the local market with the mid-cycle refresh of the compact XC40, EX40, EC40 crossover SUVs and also a flagship CUV – the long-range version of the XC90 T8 plug-in hybrid.
The Swedish automaker may not feel all too well globally with dwindling profits during the third quarter of the year, but over in the United Kingdom the local division Volvo Car UK won’t be issuing any complaints: during the third quarter of this year, Volvo registered 18,991 cars in the UK, up nearly six percent compared to last year and also nailed a September record in the process.
As such, it’s no wonder the company aims to keep up the good times by announcing the latest novelties for customers: Volvo Car UK has launched the refreshed 40 series range, which is now available for order in the country. Three models are available: the mild-hybrid XC40 , as well as the fully electric EX40 and EC40 coupe-SUV.
All three of them “feature significant design, technology and safety enhancements,” and on-the-road pricing kicks off at £37,710 (around $50k at the current exchange rate) for the XC40, from £43,860 (over $58k) for the EX40 and £45,860 (over $61k) for the EC40. The facelift brings “a more confident interpretation of Volvo’s Scandinavian design language.”
So, all three of them have redesigned front bumpers, hoods, and front wings, an upgraded grille, and new Thor’s Hammer Matrix LED headlights with 15-segment adaptive lighting technology. Around the back, the XC40 and EX40 have new LED rear lights, a revised tailgate, and a redesigned bumper, while the EC40 doesn’t have changes. The XC40 also has new diamond-cut wheels in 18-, 19- and 20-inch sizes.
Moving inside, the three refreshed siblings have a larger 11.2-inch center touchscreen with Volvo’s latest user interface, an improved wireless phone charger, premium upholstery and décor options, smart storage and “refined” cabin illumination. XC40 customers can also add Arianne Cardamom leather upholstery with Brown Ash wood.
The Volvo XC40 comes to the UK with the B3 and B4 gasoline mild-hybrid engines and a seven-speed automatic, while the EX40 has the P5 Long Range Plus specification with RWD or AWD and a range of up to 354 miles. The EC40 has the same trim for RWD but switches to P8 for AWD, and the range is up to 359 miles on a charge.
Additionally, Volvo also said it has opened the order books for the XC90 T8 Long Range plug-in hybrid flagship crossover SUV. It comes with the latest design update, “with styling that reflects Scandinavian luxury,” and the popular big CUV additionally welcomes a new long-range hybrid powertrain with up to 101 miles of electric range, which is more than double its predecessor’s performance.
UK on-the-road prices start at £66,270 (over $88k) for the B5 mild hybrid version, and the new T8 Long Range plug-in hybrid starts at £75,765 or about $101k! The T8 Long Range plug-in hybrid has a combined 461 horsepower and can sprint to 62 mph in just 5.2 seconds. Inside, there’s room for seven, an 11.2-inch center touchscreen with Volvo's latest user interface, quilted Nordico and ventilated Nappa soft leather, as well as Google Gemini, Google's conversational AI assistant, which is also offered on the refreshed 40 series.
Safety remains paramount for Volvo, with the XC90 and 40 series, with the latter gaining an updated sensor and software platform with new radar and camera technology and 12 ultrasonic sensors. The flagship SUV has Pilot Assist, adaptive cruise control, Blind Spot Information System with Steer Assist, and City Safety with automatic braking, plus Automatic Matrix LED headlights with adaptive shadow technology, among others.
